title: a-watchme-names-its-receiver
intention: A WATCHME spec names its receiver — what receives the probe's data and in which component — and a spec without one is refused at cast, at the crossing, and flagged by the at-rest ticket inspection.
why: Akien, 2026-10-01: 'I think we've just been doing 1' — probes were built and nothing receives what they send. Measured: 138 of 138 WATCHME specs name a person in prose as consumer and none names code that receives. The lived symptom: probes fire into the void, and the efficacy question a WATCHME was carried for is never answered by anything that acts on it.
traces_to: Akien's ruling, item 2 of ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md (2026-10-01). Memory a-probe-needs-a-consumer (RULED 2026-09-30): no consumer that USES the data = trash; receiver first. Law 1: watchme_present in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py is a second opinion of watchme_spec.REQUIRED_FIELDS and already disagrees (it checks 5 fields; the spec requires 7). Measured 2026-10-01: 138 of 138 WATCHME specs carry 'consumer', a prose field naming a person or role (e.g. 'CodeMother, who owns the care of the code'); 0 carry a receiver naming code in a component.
how: In cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py add RECEIVER_FIELD = 'receiver': a dict {'what': non-empty str naming the code that receives, 'in': repo-relative component directory}; watchme_spec_error faults a spec whose receiver is absent, not a dict, has an empty 'what', or whose 'in' is not a directory holding intention+why.json, naming every fault in one message. cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py's watchme_present check stops spelling its own field list and reports watchme_spec_error's text, so there is one opinion about a complete spec. The sweep tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py changes from 'no fault' to 'no fault except a missing receiver', and records the measured list of specs lacking one as the work list of the receiver-backfill ticket.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a spec complete in every current field but with no receiver passes watchme_spec_error; (2) a receiver whose 'in' is not a directory holding intention+why.json passes; (3) a receiver with an empty 'what' passes; (4) a spec with a valid receiver is refused; (5) the ticket inspector's watchme_present finding on a receiver-less fixture does not carry watchme_spec_error's text; (6) the real corpus sweep shows any fault other than a missing receiver. Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the receiver of this rule is the cast door and the crossing gate in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, which call watchme_spec_error on every ticket that carries a watch
children: none, because the receiver backfill over the 138 standing specs is its own sibling ticket cast after this one is PROVED, with its work list measured by this ticket's sweep tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) The shape? receiver = {'what': str, 'in': 'cairn/devices/codemother'}; 'in' resolved against the repo root and must contain intention+why.json. (2) Where does the fault text go? appended to the same faults list in watchme_spec_error as the REQUIRED_FIELDS faults, e.g. "WATCHME(obj) spec names no receiver — a probe with nothing that USES its data is trash (Akien, 2026-10-01)". (3) The inspector? for a ticket whose state carries WATCHME, err = watchme_spec_error(t); if err: finding('watchme_present', err).
